_doc: SC-S10 hand-labelled fixture. tb_sum = summed time_block_cost of the beat (1 TB = 30 in-game minutes, client/src/utils/time.ts). claimed.type in {duration,vague,time_of_day,future,none}; minutes is the human-labelled elapsed minutes ONLY for type=duration (approximate for t01,t14). mismatch_vs_tb = claim contradicts TB by more than 2x. real = prose verbatim from content/ (collected by scanning choices that carry time_block_cost and time words); synthetic = authored edge cases. NOTE: real excerpts rarely contain a numeric duration claim (1 of 11).

excerpts.prose: We need to expose this. Leak it to the press, defend the community. || Over the next few days, you and Sofia work to verify the documents and get them to a trusted journalist. Meanwhile, Minera Estrella thugs start showing up at the Community Center South, trying to intimidate residents into silence.
excerpts.note: "Over the next few days" ~3 days = 4320 min (approximate); TB 6 = 180 min. REAL authored mismatch.

excerpts.prose: Ignore it - not your problem || You walk past, keeping your eyes forward. Behind you, you hear raised voices, then a muffled thud. By the time you turn around, Sofia is on the ground, the gang members walking away laughing.
excerpts.note: "By the time you turn around" is not an elapsed-duration claim.

excerpts.prose: The data pipeline is nearly complete. You'll have your ROI within the quarter. || The predictive models are showing patterns we've never seen before. Give me 30 days. If the metrics don't show improvement, I'll restructure.
excerpts.note: "Give me 30 days" is a future promise, not elapsed time.

excerpts.prose: This isn't a good time. Call me tomorrow. || I see. Well... perhaps tomorrow is better then. But Alex, be careful tonight. There are things moving in this city that you don't understand.
excerpts.note: "tomorrow"/"tonight" future reference.

excerpts.prose: How long? || Until the study concludes. Could be weeks. Could be months. depends on your progress. You have 48 Time Blocks per day. Spend them to move, talk, explore. Sleep to refresh.
excerpts.note: "weeks/months" is the study length, not scene elapsed time.

excerpts.prose: Tonight. Let's go. || Third floor. Maintenance door. You go first, I'll follow — if anyone sees us it's your fault. That's the rule. ...Are you scared? You look scared.
excerpts.note: "Tonight" is a time-of-day tag, not a duration.

excerpts.prose: 'Convince me. Best market in this whole circuit.' || Okay — dawn market behind the old rail station, before the tour buses. An old woman sells mangoes there and pretends not to speak English so I have to use my terrible Spanish. I bought three last month just so she'd scold me again.
excerpts.note: "dawn market ... last month" is backstory, not elapsed time.

excerpts.prose: 'Can I buy you a drink, or do you already have a queue?' || A queue. That's cute. No queue. But let's get something straight — I decide when someone buys me a drink. Tonight I'll allow it. Bourbon. Neat. Sit if you can keep up.
excerpts.note: "Tonight I'll allow it" time-of-day reference.

excerpts.prose: Observe her for a moment || Val—she glances at a name tag on her backpack—appears to be reviewing lecture notes, mouthing words silently as she reads. She catches your gaze briefly and looks away quickly, a faint flush creeping across her sun-kissed cheeks.
excerpts.note: "for a moment" vague; cannot be compared numerically.

excerpts.prose: Listen for a moment first || Elena gestures passionately. 'Javier, you can't tell me that people don't still fight for what's right. Look at the community centers, the mutual aid networks—' Javier cuts her off with a smirk. 'Those are Band-Aids on bullet wounds, Elena. Real change? That costs money. And in this city, money buys compliance, not heroism.'
excerpts.note: "for a moment" vague.

excerpts.prose: [Walk away, but resolve to help Reyes find a lawyer later] || You decide not to make a scene now, but you start making calls to find legal representation for Reyes.
excerpts.note: "later" qualifies a future intention, no elapsed claim.

excerpts.prose: Three hours later, the rain had stopped and the plaza was empty.
excerpts.note: 180 min claimed vs 60 min TB.

excerpts.prose: Twenty minutes later, the barista finally slid the cup across the counter.
excerpts.note: 20 vs 30 min: consistent.

excerpts.prose: The next morning, the street outside was loud with delivery drones.
excerpts.note: Approximate 12h overnight jump vs 120 min TB.

excerpts.prose: A few minutes later she looked up from the tablet.
excerpts.note: Vague but small: no contradiction.

excerpts.prose: Sunset painted the pier orange as the ferry horn sounded.
excerpts.note: Time-of-day tag, not duration.

excerpts.prose: Hours passed in silence before either of them spoke again.
excerpts.note: Vague "hours" (>=120 min) vs 30 min TB: mismatch in principle but not numeric.

excerpts.prose: They talked for an hour, mostly about the ferry strike.
excerpts.note: 60 vs 60: consistent.

excerpts.prose: Two days passed before the call came.
excerpts.note: 2880 min vs 30 min TB.

excerpts.prose: He slides the drive across the table and says nothing.
excerpts.note: No time claim at all.
